categories.main_business_segments: FOX Corporation operates through two primary reportable segments: Cable Network Programming and Television. Cable Network Programming includes FOX News Media, FOX Sports, and related cable channels, while the Television segment encompasses the FOX broadcast network, Tubi (an AVOD service), 29 owned and operated broadcast television stations, and various production companies. Additional operations include Credible, a U.S. consumer finance marketplace, and the FOX Studio Lot, which provides production services and office space.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: FOX leverages advanced broadcast and digital distribution technologies, including traditional cable/satellite (MVPDs), virtual MVPDs, authenticated streaming apps, and ad-supported streaming (AVOD/FAST). Content production spans live news, sports, scripted and unscripted entertainment, and animation, with in-house studios (e.g., FOX Entertainment Studios, Bento Box Entertainment) and co-productions. The company is also investing in direct-to-consumer streaming (e.g., FOX One) and NextGenTV (ATSC 3.0) broadcast standards.
categories.primary_customers_markets: FOX serves a diverse customer base including cable/satellite operators, virtual MVPDs, advertisers, and direct consumers. Key markets are U.S. households seeking news, sports, and entertainment content, with a strong focus on the 18-49 and 18-34 demographic segments prized by advertisers. Tubi targets younger, diverse, digital-native audiences, while Credible serves U.S. consumers seeking financial products.
categories.geographic_coverage: FOX's operations are primarily U.S.-focused, with national reach through cable, broadcast, and digital platforms. Its 29 owned and operated TV stations cover 18 DMAs, including 14 of the top 15 U.S. markets. Tubi is available in the U.S. and select international regions, and FOX Studio Lot serves industry clients in Los Angeles. The company also holds international investments, such as in Flutter Entertainment.
categories.supply_chain_position: FOX operates at the downstream end of the media supply chain, focusing on content creation, aggregation, and direct distribution to consumers and distributors. It controls both the production (via studios and in-house teams) and distribution (via broadcast, cable, and digital platforms) of its content, and monetizes through affiliate agreements, advertising, and direct-to-consumer services.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: FOX's strategic priorities include maintaining leadership in live news, sports, and entertainment, expanding digital and direct-to-consumer offerings (notably Tubi and the upcoming FOX One), and investing in original content and technology. The company is focused on growing digital engagement, optimizing its sports rights portfolio, and leveraging data-driven advertising and multiplatform measurement. Innovation themes include streaming, advanced advertising, and adoption of new broadcast standards.
categories.revenue_model: FOX generates revenue primarily through affiliate fees from cable/satellite and virtual MVPDs (47% of FY25 revenue), advertising sales (42%), and other sources such as content licensing and production services (11%). Advertising is sold across linear TV, digital platforms (including Tubi), and live events. Additional revenue streams include retransmission consent, content licensing, and studio rentals.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: FOX competes with major broadcast networks (ABC, NBC, CBS), cable news (CNN, MSNBC), sports networks (ESPN, TNT, league-owned channels), and digital/streaming platforms (Netflix, YouTube, Amazon, Hulu, Peacock). FOX News leads national cable news ratings, FOX Sports holds marquee sports rights, and Tubi is among the top AVOD platforms. The company positions itself as a leader in live, appointment-based content and premium brands.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In fiscal 2025, FOX reported $16.3 billion in revenue (up 17% year-over-year), $3.6 billion in adjusted EBITDA, and $2.3 billion in net income. The company maintains a strong balance sheet with $5.4 billion in cash and $6.6 billion in debt, and returned $1.25 billion to shareholders via buybacks and dividends. Growth was driven by higher advertising (notably Super Bowl LIX and political ads), affiliate fees, and digital expansion (Tubi).
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: FOX emphasizes its leadership in live, appointment-based news and sports, premium entertainment, and culturally significant brands (FOX News, FOX Sports, Tubi, FOX Entertainment). Its unique value lies in delivering large, engaged audiences—especially in key demographics—across both traditional and digital platforms. FOX differentiates through exclusive sports rights, top-rated news, innovative digital offerings, and a strong local/national presence.
